ElementDescription: The NDAR Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for research subject
Subject ID how it's defined in lab/project
Date on which the interview/genetic test/sampling/imaging/biospecimen was completed. MM/DD/YYYY
Age in months at the time of the interview/test/sampling/imaging.
Notes: Age is rounded to chronological month. If the research participant is 15-days-old at time of interview, the appropriate value would be 0 months. If the participant is 16-days-old, the value would be 1 month.
M = Male; F = Female; O=Other; NR = Not reported

ElementDescription: Family level ID how it is defined in the lab/project. Same family ID used for parent and adolescent
Timepoint out of four assessments: Time 1 (baseline) - Time 2 (8-month follow-up) - Time 3 (16-month follow-up) - Time 4 (24-month follow-up)
Continuous Assessment of Interpersonal Dynamics - Time in seconds for ratings
Continuous Assessment of Interpersonal Dynamics - Aggregated coder ratings of warmth-coldness dimension
Notes: Higher scores reflect greater warmth which is reflected by both verbal statements, such as support, praise, laughing, complimenting, as well as non-verbal behaviors such as eye contact, affectionate touching, moving closer together

ElementDescription: Continuous Assessment of Interpersonal Dynamics - Aggregated coder ratings of dominance-submissive dimension
Notes: Higher scores reflect greater dominance which is indicated by behaviors such as asserting authority, directing the topic of conversation, taking an imposing posture
